Title: Block opportunity on a redirected Bleed that returns to original target

Messages.Author: Ceemitere
Messages.Body:
Hi everyone,

I have a quick clarification request regarding block opportunities and redirection chains on a Bleed action.

Scenario:

Player A bleeds Player B.

Player B plays a reaction card to wake (e.g., On the Qui Vive) and plays a redirection card (Telepathic Misdirection / Deflection) to pass the Bleed to Player C, without declaring a block attempt.

Player C then plays Deflection and redirects the Bleed back to Player B.

Question:
Does Player B gain a new opportunity to attempt a block against this same Bleed action once it is redirected back to them (assuming they didn't attempt a block earlier, just redirected)?

My understanding is that once Player B declines/passes their natural block opportunity in order to redirect the action, they cannot attempt a normal block if the action returns to them, unless they use a card that explicitly instructs a vampire to attempt a block (like Second Tradition: Domain). Is this correct?

Thanks in advance!

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:
From roolbook:
"If the target of the action is changed (e.g. a bleed action is redirected), this will reopen block attempts, following the normal rules."

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> mipopo3 wrote:
> From roolbook:
> "If the target of the action is changed (e.g. a bleed action is redirected), this will reopen block attempts, following the normal rules."
>
Correct.
